skill.description: Automates Claude Code hook setup for pre-task, post-edit, session, Git, memory, and MCP coordination workflows.
skill.summary: Configure Claude Code hooks for workflow automation, agent coordination, memory persistence, and quality checks.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command examples, and documentation-only shell snippets. The main security issue is that several hook configuration examples interpolate tool parameters into shell command strings, which can create command injection risk if copied directly.

remediation.issue: Hook command examples interpolate untrusted tool parameters into shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Rewrite examples to call a small wrapper script that receives values as JSON or environment variables, then validates and escapes arguments before invoking claude-flow.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes many executable shell examples without clear safety boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Mark commands as examples, add a review warning before installing hooks, and avoid destructive examples such as rm -rf even when demonstrating safety checks.

remediation.issue: Examples reference sensitive environment files in hook flows.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the protected-file example, but explicitly state that hooks should block edits to environment files and must never log their contents.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Command Injection in Hook Configuration Examples
semantic_findings.description: The hook configuration examples place tool parameters such as file paths, Bash commands, task text, and search patterns directly inside shell command strings. Users who copy these examples can expose their hooks to command injection when those values contain shell metacharacters.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples show direct interpolation like ${tool.params.file_path}, ${tool.params.command}, and pattern-derived paths inside shell command fields. Claude Code hook commands execute through a shell, so copied examples can become injection-prone.

content.value_statement: Manual hook setup can be hard to coordinate across agents, sessions, Git, and memory tools. This skill provides structured examples for Claude Code hook automation with Claude Flow and MCP workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains pre-operation hooks for edit, Bash, task, and search preparation.
Shows post-operation hooks for formatting, metrics, memory updates, and pattern training.
Provides Claude Code settings examples for PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, and SessionEnd hooks.
Documents Git hook workflows for pre-commit, post-commit, and pre-push quality gates.
Describes MCP memory coordination patterns for swarm agents and sessions.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for hook execution, timeouts, memory, and performance.
limitations: Requires Claude Flow CLI and compatible Claude Code hook configuration.
Examples must be reviewed before use because some interpolate tool parameters into shell commands.
Does not provide a packaged implementation file beyond the documentation.
MCP and swarm features require separately configured servers and permissions.

use_cases.title: Standardize team hook setup
use_cases.description: Create a shared Claude Code hook configuration for formatting, validation, and session tracking.

use_cases.title: Coordinate multi-agent workflows
use_cases.description: Use hook events to store task context, update agent state, and persist decisions across sessions.

use_cases.title: Add Git quality gates
use_cases.description: Connect pre-commit and pre-push checks to validation, formatting, tests, and reporting flows.

prompt_templates.title: Start basic hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the hooks-automation skill to explain the simplest safe Claude Code hook setup for my project.

prompt_templates.title: Configure edit hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Using hooks-automation, draft a safe PreToolUse and PostToolUse plan for validating and formatting edited files.

prompt_templates.title: Design session memory flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use hooks-automation to design a session-start and session-end workflow that saves summaries and restores context.

prompt_templates.title: Audit advanced hook automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed Claude Code hook configuration using hooks-automation and identify command injection or secret logging risks.

output_examples.input: Set up hooks for a small JavaScript project.
output_examples.output: A recommended hook plan with edit validation, post-edit formatting, test triggers, and notes about safe argument handling.

output_examples.input: Coordinate three agents during a refactor.
output_examples.output: A staged workflow using pre-task preparation, memory keys, post-task summaries, and session persistence.
A checklist covering timeout settings, async hooks, command performance, MCP connectivity, and debug logs.

best_practices: Review every hook command before enabling it in a shared repository.
Use wrapper scripts or structured inputs instead of direct shell interpolation.
Keep hooks fast, observable, and limited to the minimum required automation.
anti_patterns: Do not copy shell interpolation examples into production without escaping and validation.
Do not log secrets, environment file contents, or full command output by default.
Do not make heavy checks block every tool call when asynchronous hooks would work.

faq.question: What does this skill help automate?
faq.answer: It helps plan Claude Code hooks for validation, formatting, memory coordination, session persistence, Git checks, and MCP workflows.

faq.question: Does it install hooks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and settings examples that users must adapt and review before enabling.

faq.question: Which tools does it reference?
faq.answer: It references Claude, Codex, Claude Code, Claude Flow CLI, Git hooks, and MCP coordination tools.

faq.question: Is it safe to copy every example directly?
faq.answer: No. Some examples interpolate parameters into shell commands and should be rewritten with safer argument handling.

faq.question: Can it coordinate swarm agents?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation describes memory keys, session hooks, and MCP events for multi-agent coordination.

faq.question: What should I review first?
faq.answer: Review shell commands, environment-file handling, logging behavior, timeouts, and permissions before enabling hooks.
